Also, do the symptoms feel clearly tied to the exam failure and other stressors?\n\nPatient: It’s been incredibly hard to function—I’m making more charting errors at work, had to postpone my next exam attempt because I can't focus to study, and I'm dodging calls from my family because I have no energy. These feelings are definitely tied to failing that exam, combined with the constant pressure of our understaffed clinic.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a similar period of depression or loss of interest before this, even if it was milder or not tied to a specific stressor?\n\nPatient: No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've ever felt a depression or loss of interest like this, and it feels entirely new and completely overwhelming to me.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within a month of the exam failure and other stressors, or did they begin later and seem unrelated to those events?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started almost immediately, just a couple of days after I found out I failed the exam three weeks ago. It definitely didn't start later—it hit me right then and has been weighing on me constantly ever since.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of actually harming yourself or making a plan to end your life, or are the thoughts more about not wanting to be here without a plan?\n\nPatient: It started with just wishing I wouldn't wake up, but lately I've spent time online reading about painless methods of dying and picturing myself doing it. I don't have a concrete plan set in motion, but it really scares me because it feels much more serious than just a passing thought.\n\nDoctor: Have you been having any symptoms like intrusive memories, nightmares, feeling on edge, or avoiding reminders of the exam failure or the hurricane-related stress? Or is it mainly a persistent depressed mood and loss of interest without those trauma-related symptoms?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge or jumpy. It is really just this persistent, heavy depressed mood and a complete loss of interest in things I used to love like painting and salsa. Instead of feeling highly anxious or on alert, I just feel completely hollow, exhausted, physically slowed down, and empty inside.\n\nDoctor: Have these symptoms been improving at all since the stressor, or have they stayed severe and constant every day for more than two weeks? This is also the very first time I have ever experienced anything like this, as I've never had a similar episode before.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks when there was no major stressor or trigger, or has this episode only happened after the exam failure and other stressors?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had anything like this happen before; this is the very first time I've ever felt this way. It only started about three weeks ago, right after I failed my certification exam and was dealing with the intense stress and understaffing at the clinic.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms been improving at all as the stress from the exam and work has changed, or do they stay just as severe even when you are away from those stressors?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't improved at all and stay just as severe. They have been weighing on me constantly without letting up for the past three weeks, even when I am away from work or trying to relax at home. It feels like there is no escape from this heavy feeling, no matter where I am or what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, or were more talkative, impulsive, or overly confident than usual?\n\nPatient: No, I have never experienced a period of feeling unusually energized, irritable, or overly confident like that. My feelings have mostly been the exact opposite—heavy, slow, and completely exhausted.\n\nDoctor: Have you been having trouble sleeping, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual since this started? I'm also dodging calls and invites from my friends and family because I just don't have the energy to show up for anyone anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms been improving at all as the stressor changes, or do they remain severe even when you are away from the exam and work stress?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't improved at all and remain just as severe. My struggle has been much more about the heavy sadness, my complete lack of energy, and those dark thoughts about not wanting to be here anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms been steadily present most days for at least two weeks even when you are away from the stressor, or do they mainly come and go only when you are dealing with the stressful situation?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have been steadily present every single day for about three weeks now, without letting up at all. It is a continuous, heavy weight that stays with me even when I am at home or away from the clinic and studying, rather than something that just comes and goes. It is just always there, no matter what.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms begin within a month of the stressful event and seem clearly tied to it, or have they continued for months or appeared without a clear trigger?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started about three weeks ago, directly after I found out I failed my key certification exam. It felt completely tied to that failure, especially coming on top of the intense stress at the clinic, and the feelings have been constant and unyielding ever since.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks before this, even when nothing major was going on in your life?"

Before the exam failure and the intense stress at the clinic, I was always very active with my yoga, painting, and salsa dancing. These feelings only started about three weeks ago after I got those results.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start only after the exam failure and other stress, or did you have a period of low mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks before that without a clear trigger?\n\nPatient: No, I didn't have any period of low mood or loss of interest before the exam. The constant heavy feeling and losing interest in everything only took hold about three weeks ago, right after I found out I failed.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any major stressors or traumatic events around the time these symptoms started, and did the low mood and loss of interest begin within a few days of that event?\n\nPatient: Yes, finding out I failed that certification exam was the major trigger, on top of the stress of helping displaced patients at my understaffed clinic after the hurricane season. This is the very first time I've ever felt a depression or loss of interest like this, and it feels entirely new and completely overwhelming to me.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within a month of the exam failure and other stressors, or did they begin later and seem unrelated to those events?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started almost immediately, just a couple of days after I found out I failed the exam three weeks ago.
